# World Models for Manipulation — Survey

World Models for Robotic Manipulation: A Survey

**2026-08-31 · SmartBot · Review article · Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Great Bay University; HIT Shenzhen; HKU; KTH and collaborators**

**[Paper](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)**

A manipulation-focused review organizes world models by predicted representation, action interface and learning lifecycle.

| Field | Reported value and source scope |
| :-- | :-- |
| Record type | Survey |
| Review scope | Predictive systems for robotic manipulation, including spatial, contact and physical dynamics. [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |
| Organizing taxonomy | Image/video · Latent dynamics · Flow/scene motion · 3D/4D geometry · Physics-informed dynamics [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |
| Adaptation mechanisms | Integrated prediction–action, predictive planning, policy augmentation and learned-environment improvement across pretraining, post-training and inference. [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |
| Context and evidence | World-grounded, intervention-aware predictions; observations and robot actions constrain future scene/contact evolution. [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |
| Evaluation dimensions | Prediction quality · Task performance · Contact plausibility · Action alignment · Simulator reliability [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |
| Literature corpus and snapshot | Publisher bibliography has 162 references; review describes 38 manipulation datasets. Published online August 31, 2026. [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |
| Literature selection | Functional taxonomy linking representations, predictive cores, action interfaces, infrastructure roles and lifecycle stages. [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |
| Coverage boundaries | Pure perception, inverse models, policies without prediction and standalone utility functions are outside its operational world-model definition. Dataset references are not independent policy results. [1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053)  |

**Scope and qualifications**

- No direct robot policy, control frequency or training-resource claim belongs to this review.

**Primary evidence**

1. [Publisher full text, metadata and bibliography](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/smb2.70053) — Sections1–9; author-defined taxonomy and original publication date. Geometry citations are discovery leads, not evidence for the methods themselves.
